notes: Access: direct HTTP fetch (curl_cffi, Shopify storefront) worked throughout, no block encountered. Site is Shopify + Bloomreach (dxpapi widget); PLP HTML ships an empty product grid client-rendered by Bloomreach, so qty was verified via /collections/<handle>/products.json?limit=250 pagination counting distinct product ids (same validated cross-check method as this site's prior Home-Decor pass). Navigation discovery: homepage mega-menu explicitly lists 8 room/category-scoped 'New Arrivals' links (Living Room, Dining Room, Bedroom, Lighting, Decor, Rugs, Office, Outdoor New Arrivals) plus a top-level 'SHOP EVERYTHING NEW' link to /collections/new-arrivals - this matches genuine site-defined sub-structure per the shared engine's grouping rule, so the parent + 8 children are all emitted. Cross-checked against sitemap_collections_1.xml (524 handles): found the same 8 child handles plus a duplicate handle /collections/decor-new-arrivals-1 - verified by full products.json id-set comparison that decor-new-arrivals and decor-new-arrivals-1 are byte-for-byte the same 85-product set (identical id sets), so decor-new-arrivals-1 is a true alias and was dropped, keeping only the canonical decor-new-arrivals (the one actually linked from the nav). Every row was opened and confirmed to be a real product listing, not an editorial/campaign page: each has its own descriptive <title> (e.g. 'Living Room New Arrivals - Arhaus', 'Decor New Arrivals - Arhaus') and matching <h1>, and each returns real, distinct product ids via products.json (not zero, not a lookbook). The parent /collections/new-arrivals page itself has title 'New Arrivals, New Looks, New Collections | Arhaus' and H1 'New Arrivals' - opened and confirmed it is a genuine browsable PLP (products.json returns 639 distinct ids), not merely an editorial 'New Collection' campaign page, so it passes the Collection-page test in the brief; its count (639) exceeds the sum of the 8 room children (544) because it is the sitewide superset while the children are room-scoped cross-cuts - both genuine, kept as parent+children per Rule 0 overlap guidance rather than dropped as duplicative. No other 'new'-prefixed handles in the sitemap represented New Arrivals (new-traditional, the-new-england-edit, newport were false substring matches on unrelated product-line/collection names, opened and confirmed not to be New Arrivals PLPs). Also probed /collections/new-in, new-products, just-in, just-arrived, latest-arrivals, whats-new, new, new-this-season, recently-added directly - all 404, confirming the mega-menu + sitemap set above is complete.
